scope: Independent read-only review of synchronous readonly borrowed-context callback implementation, generic signature handling, region/effect/alias checks, invoke metadata, VM/native binding and cleanup, and authored tests.
conclusion: No concrete safety or correctness defect identified in reviewed changes. This is source-review evidence, not proof of memory safety or release acceptance.

observations.finding: Borrowed versus value and slice versus whole-context bits participate in concrete and generic signature identity. Mutable callback contexts, borrowed callback returns and borrowed host parameters are rejected. Function values store target identity, not context references.

Concrete and generic indirect calls require active reference names, exact type and reference kind. Overlapping loans involving exclusive references are rejected; generic reference lookup preserves suspended-parent restrictions. Value arguments continue through ordinary ownership checking.

Concrete invoke result dependencies now include region-carrying borrowed argument owners. Generic invocation records region reads through the same borrowed context, preventing returned allocator/arena-derived values from evading the direct-call region rules.
Indirect invocation contributes the declared callback effect mask. Target ceilings remain exact contract matches; effect checks therefore cover generic noalloc callers and reject widening.

Invoke carries readonly reference IDs separately from value operands. Validation checks count, ID bounds, type, slice kind, and callable bitmask validity. Stack consumption uses only value parameters. Dynamic target checks include the complete callable contract before dispatch.

Indirect callbacks use the existing direct-call frame/reference machinery. VM creates shared child leases; native dispatch binds readonly child references after entering the target frame. Ordinary return and failure cleanup paths are reused rather than introducing retained context storage.

Context is explicitly forwarded to the comparator/predicate. Heapsort avoids quadratic sorting, lower-bound follows comparator order, and in-place filter preserves survivor order. Callbacks may trap; these algorithms do not promise transactional rollback.

coverage: Readonly record and slice contexts through generic noalloc helpers.
Wrong kinds, mutable callback declarations, writes through readonly references, duplicate exclusive loans, concrete/generic arena escapes, escaping reference returns and effect mismatch rejections.
Malformed invoke reference counts and out-of-range reference IDs; legacy dynamic signature mismatch tests remain.
Compile/format/VM/C-emission allocation-failure exercise now includes generic borrowed context.
JSON-ID comparator sorting with explicit tie-breaks, lower-bound, stable filtering and empty ranges.
Native O0/O2 plus UBSan and allocation-failure cleanup driver; separate 16,384-entry sorted-order fixture.
limits: Reviewer did not run tests or independently inspect full-suite execution logs. Parent reports focused/root coverage; release integration remains separate.

No dedicated successful fixture was identified for multiple readonly contexts interleaved with value parameters in one callback signature; implementation loops appear to preserve ordering, but such a test would strengthen coverage.
Callback-specific native trap and borrowed aggregate/region-return combinations are not exhaustively enumerated by these fixtures.
